Widen the orchestration test bounds that host load can exceed (#284)

TODO 254 records that the tests that give a normally ending enumerator
a 5 second timeout were not swept for load sensitivity, and that under
host load the timeout could cut short a child that should end
normally. The hook starts the enumerator's timeout clock when it
starts the child (subprocess.run at aiqt_hooks.py:22833), so that
timeout also covers interpreter start-up. This closes TODO 254.

tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py:

- ENUM_TIMEOUT, 60 seconds, the hook's own fallback
  (aiqt_hooks.py:22831), replaces 5 at the 3 fixture registries whose
  enumerator should end normally: stage2(), _arm_writing_enumerator
  and the doctor disclosure case. The 2 registries whose argv is
  malformed by design keep 5, since no child starts there.
- RUN_TIMEOUT, 120 seconds, bounds each test run that can start the
  enumerator of a fixture registry once: run_hook, run_doctor, the 2
  direct preflight runs, Doctor.SPECIAL_TIMEOUT (was 30),
  DoctorCheckpointWrites.TIMEOUT (was 30) and the new
  DoctorStandInRestore.TIMEOUT (was 60). The fault-injection run of
  DoctorCheckpointWrites can start it twice and keeps twice the bound,
  240 seconds. So every test bound around such a run is at least 120
  seconds, and each exceeds ENUM_TIMEOUT, once for each enumerator run
  it can hold, by at least ENUM_MARGIN, 60 seconds, so the hook's own
  timeout ends an enumerator that hangs before a test bound ends the
  run.
- run_doctor_recorded, the 1 launcher of the suite, holds the timeout
  that each launch was given, however the case bound it, to the
  enumerator starts that the launch made. It names a new file of the
  launch's own in ORCH_STAGE2_ENUMERATOR_RUNS in the launch's
  environment, and every enumerator that a case declares first runs
  ENUM_RUN_MARK, which adds 1 line to that file. However the launch
  ends, the recorder counts the lines, and a launch whose timeout is
  under ENUM_TIMEOUT for each start plus ENUM_MARGIN fails its case in
  its cleanup, or at once when no case is running. A launch with no
  start, or with no timeout, is not held.
- Stage2Harness.write_registry refuses an enumerator that the hook
  would start unless it runs python3 -I on a program file or a -c
  program that holds ENUM_RUN_MARK, and unless its timeout, as the
  hook reads it, is at most ENUM_TIMEOUT.
- The reading of launch bounds from the syntax tree is removed, with
  UNENUMERATED_RUNS and REPEATED_ENUMERATOR_RUNS. EnumeratorBounds
  requires that a stage-2 Stop and preflight each record 1 start and a
  stage-1 Stop none; that a launch 1 second under its bound fails its
  case and a launch at its bound passes, for 1 start and for 2, also
  when check=True fails, and that one with no running case fails at
  once; and that write_registry refuses an enumerator without the
  record, one run without -I, and a timeout over ENUM_TIMEOUT.
- DoctorCheckpointWrites._doctor drops a timeout parameter that no
  caller passes.
- In the enumerator timeout case the bound on the hook run goes from
  15 to 90 seconds and the sleep of its enumerator from 30 to 100
  seconds, so a hook that waited the sleep out still fails the case.

tools/test-orch-enumerate-backlog.py:

- ENUMERATE_PROG runs the real enumerator under a 60 second timeout
  instead of 5.
- The new case test_hook_ends_an_enumerator_that_does_not_end runs a
  90 second sleep through ENUMERATE_PROG under a 120 second bound and
  requires ENUMERATOR_ERROR with "timed out after 60 seconds".
- The stamp test, renamed
  test_generated_at_utc_is_stamped_while_the_enumerator_runs, requires
  that the stamp lie between the clock before the run, truncated to
  the second, and the clock after it. The enumerator truncates its
  stamp to whole seconds, so the lower bound is exact, and the test
  refuses a stale stamp that the old window accepted.
- InputFileType.TIMEOUT, the bound on each direct enumerator run of
  that class, goes from 20 to 60 seconds, the timeout ENUMERATE_PROG
  gives the enumerator, and its failure message says only that the
  enumerator did not exit within that bound.

tools/test-orchestration-registry.py is unchanged: its timeouts of 5
are data that the registry gate checks, no child runs under them, and
the gate refuses any timeout outside (0, 8]. The test registries of
the 2 changed suites never reach the gate.

Checks, run from the repository root with python3 -I: the stage-2,
enumerate-backlog and registry suites each end OK, and the label suite
ends OK in a git checkout. With 1 edit in a copy of the tree, a 6 s
start-up delay of the fixture enumerator fails 4 stage-2 cases on
main's test files and none with this change; a 6 s delay of the real
enumerator fails the hook case and the stamp test on main's files and
neither with this change; a 21 s delay of the real enumerator fails
the large-input InputFileType case on main's files and not with this
change, and a 61 s delay fails it with this change; a 50 s delay of
the hook fails the enumerator timeout case's old 15 s bound and passes
its 90 s bound. Controls: a 91 s hook delay fails the 90 s bound, an
enumerator stamp 3 s stale fails the new stamp test, and a 100 s
timeout in ENUMERATE_PROG fails the new hang case. With this change, a
new Doctor case whose preflight launch has a timeout of 30, through a
local RUN_TIMEOUT, through an alias of run_doctor_recorded with a
mapping, or in a class outside the harness, fails, and passes with
RUN_TIMEOUT; DoctorStandInRestore fails with self.TIMEOUT set to 30
before its launch, and the planted-module case fails with the bounds
of its 2 launches swapped. EnumeratorBounds fails when the check never
reports, drops ENUM_MARGIN or ignores the number of starts, when the
recorder names the file in another variable, and when write_registry
skips its check. With a fixture enumerator that sleeps 70 s, no case
of the stage-2 harness ends through a test bound; with the earlier
bounds, 4 doctor cases do. With 64 busy processes and the enumerator
timeout case pinned to 1 CPU, the case is expected to end OK in each
of 3 runs.

Residuals: a wider bound makes a load failure rarer, not impossible.
An enumerator that hangs holds a test run for up to 60 s, a doctor or
hook run that blocks fails after 120 s instead of 30, and a direct
enumerator run of InputFileType that blocks fails after 60 s instead
of 20. The new hang case adds 60 s to the enumerate-backlog suite.
The bound check counts only starts that an enumerator records: a
registry written other than through write_registry, a program changed
after it, and a child that drops ORCH_STAGE2_ENUMERATOR_RUNS from its
environment are not seen. It holds only the starts a launch made when
a case ran it, not a start recorded after the launch returned, and not
a launch with no timeout. The fixture value 60 is safe only while the
test registries are never gated. The new stamp test fails on a
backward clock step during the run. The load check covers only the
enumerator timeout case and CPU contention.
